title: ACIS reader independence and executable qualification routes
mode: Primary-source product/documentation review, published peer-reader scope review, and reconciliation with existing local qualification receipts; plan-only
worktreeState: Dirty shared worktree; preserved all existing changes; no production or test code modified
questions: Does the selected official macOS ARM64 CAD Assistant package provide an executable independent ACIS-reader route, and what are its kernel, license, and result-output boundaries?
Which open-source readers can decode the exact ACIS carrier as distinct parser implementations, and which can establish shape semantics or kernel validity?
What identity and ownership evidence is still needed to join a standalone SAB result back to its DWG/AcDs source?

sources.name: Open CASCADE CAD Assistant product page
sources.observed: Vendor docs list SAT/SAB import through commercial OCCT XDE components, state that the free CAD Assistant app permits this import while disallowing model export/conversion, expose selected part area/volume/centroid properties, and currently point to version 1.6.0 dated 2021. The page's previous 1.5.0 entry explicitly lists macOS ARM64; exact architecture must be established from the artifact actually tested.

sources.name: Open CASCADE commercial components preview and announcement
sources.observed: ACIS SAT/SAB exchange is a commercial component, not a standard open-source OCCT codec. CAD Assistant is a distinct ACIS reader from libdxfrw but its shape construction is in the OCCT kernel family, which is shared with FreeCAD.

sources.name: cq-acis project and acis-core API
sources.observed: The project calls itself experimental, documents bounded SAT/SAB/ASM profiles, retains unsupported records, and converts supported geometry through CadQuery/OCCT. acis-core validates reference closure and source ranges but does not construct OCCT solids; it is part of the same cq-acis parser/model lineage, not a second independent parser vote. The test corpus is excluded from Python packages and has separate license notices.

sources.name: cadmpeg-codec-sat published documentation and architecture
sources.observed: The published 0.6.1 crate describes a read-only bare-stream decoder that transfers supported geometry into neutral IR, reports losses/unknown records, and verifies Spatial ACIS bands 217/218. It does not parse the DWG/DXF container, write SAT/SAB, or supply a CAD kernel. Treat the package's own coverage claims as scope documentation, not correctness evidence.

sources.name: Existing local qualification record
sources.observed: The existing record says one hash-pinned SAB attempt with official CAD Assistant ended in a transfer error without geometry or metrics, and the downloaded app bundle failed strict code-signature verification. This is inconclusive and does not establish an invalid SAB; the package must pass integrity review before another launch. Existing witness-generation and exact AcDs linkage requirements remain in force.

planChanges: Separate parser independence, kernel independence, native-app acceptance, and output observability into distinct evidence columns.
Treat CAD Assistant as an optional OCCT-family black-box reader with import-only access; integrity and exact package architecture/version must be verified before execution.
Admit one exact-pinned cq-acis route per documented profile; do not count acis-core as another parser and review corpus licensing before use.
Use cadmpeg-codec-sat only as an exact-profile read-only parser/neutral-geometry cross-check, capturing its full loss report and independently expected measures.
Require the DWG entity-to-AcDs schema/index/key-to-exact-SAB-hash join separately; no standalone reader can establish that container association.

Keep BricsCAD/Ansys as optional independent-kernel candidates subject to exact profile, license, and measurable output qualification; unavailable external lanes self-unblock to the local implementation queue.
